html:
The campaign in which the Cossack leader Yermak Timofeyevich crossed the Ural Mountains and in 1582 took Qashliq, the capital of the Khanate of Sibir. It began the Russian conquest of Siberia.

Yermak was hired by the Stroganovs, a merchant family with lands in the Urals, to fight raids from Sibir. With a few hundred Cossacks armed with guns, he sailed up the rivers and over the mountains, and in October 1582 beat the forces of Khan Kuchum on the Irtysh River. He offered the conquest to Tsar Ivan the Terrible. In 1585 Kuchum's men ambushed him, and he drowned in the Irtysh.

Moscow sent troops and built forts such as Tobolsk in 1587. Cossacks and fur traders then moved east along the rivers, and reached the Pacific at Okhotsk in 1639. The Russian conquest of Siberia made Russia a state that stretched across Asia. Yermak became a folk hero.
